label_status: Provisional author-labelled diagnostic examples; not independent labels or a held-out benchmark. Thresholds were fixed before the live run.

prices.text: During the summer of 2024, most bidding zones in Southeast Europe saw a significant increase in electricity prices, particularly during the evening hours, reaching values of up to 1000 EUR/MWh. During these high-price events, price spreads at several bidding zone borders in Central Europe rose to unprecedented levels, signalling insufficient availability of cross-zonal capacity to accommodate all the market’s need for cross-zonal exchanges. This is summarised in Figure 1.
prices.title: ACER Increasing Cross-Zonal Capacity and System Flexibility in Southeast Europe 2026

capacity.text: In the EU, the main regulatory tool to ensure the maximisation of cross-zonal capacities is the 70% requirement, introduced in the Electricity Regulation. It requires TSOs to offer at least 70% of their physical capacity on all relevant lines for cross-zonal trade, while complying wi th safety standards of secure network operation. This requirement was introduced to address the discrimination of cross-zonal exchanges in favour of intra-zonal exchanges, inherent to a zonal market design.
capacity.title: ACER Increasing Cross-Zonal Capacity and System Flexibility in Southeast Europe 2026

proposals.text: This second section sets out several targeted measures aimed at improving the operational processes and network infrastructure that affect cross-zonal trade within Southeast Europe, as well as between Southeast Europe and the rest of the EU. If implemented, these measures could increase cross-zonal capacity in the short to medium term and improve the ability of imports from the rest of the EU to alleviate prices in Southeast Europe.
proposals.title: ACER Increasing Cross-Zonal Capacity and System Flexibility in Southeast Europe 2026
